elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Total external debt, 2015–25
elements.description: Total external debt rises throughout 2015–25, from 38,440 to 74,384 US$ million. The lowest printed value is in 2015 and the highest is in 2025.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.description: Nested stacked bars break down total external debt in 2025, with shaded connectors linking public and publicly guaranteed debt to its creditor types and linking multilateral and bilateral debt to their components. Private nonguaranteed debt is the largest top-level component, while short-term debt is the smallest. Among public and publicly guaranteed creditor types, multilateral is largest and private creditors smallest; World Bank-IDA is the largest multilateral component and Japan the smallest bilateral component.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 3
elements.title: Debt ratios, 2015–25
legend: 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries (shaded band)
elements.description: Four small line charts show external debt and debt service relative to exports and GNI from 2015 to 2025. Both debt service ratios have a pronounced spike followed by a decline. In 2025, external debt / exports is the highest displayed ratio at 787%, and debt service / GNI is the lowest at 22%.
elements.notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025
elements.description: Two side-by-side boxes show average terms for official and private creditors in 2025. The official creditors box lists maturity of 13 years, grace period of 13 years and interest rate of 5.4%, with small bars beneath each measure. The private creditors box lists maturity, grace period and interest rate as '..', with empty bars beneath them.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database. Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025.
